subject.title: [Architecture] Extract terminal execution drivers from agent-core packages

question: Should terminal process execution become a reusable terminal-core contract, or remain owned by the existing exec/runtime layer while the RuntimePlan RFC handles runner decomposition?
rationale: The choice changes ownership of security-sensitive execution behavior and cannot be inferred safely from the short proposal or partially overlapping RFC.

options.title: Keep Runtime Ownership
options.body: Keep approvals, sandboxing, spawning, lifecycle, and result handling in the existing exec/runtime owner while limiting the RFC to internal runner decomposition.

options.title: Design Driver Contract
options.body: Sponsor a separate package-boundary design that names consumers and preserves approval, sandbox, environment, cancellation, and process-tree contracts.

options.title: Fold Into RFC
options.body: Add a scoped terminal-driver investigation to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72072 before deciding whether a separate package is warranted.

recommendation.title: Keep Runtime Ownership
recommendation.body: Keep approvals, sandboxing, spawning, lifecycle, and result handling in the existing exec/runtime owner while limiting the RFC to internal runner decomposition.

likelyOwner.reason: The active RFC already owns the adjacent runner-finalization roadmap and is the clearest place to reconcile the overlap.
